This is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned about﴾ [Qur'an 17:36].

Abu Jaʿfar said: it is well-being (al-ʿafiya).

ʿAqil informed me, saying: al-Muʿafa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Ibn Humayd informed us, saying: Mihran narrated to us from Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi, from Thabit al-Bunani, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The bounty that will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection is a morsel of bread that sustains you, water that quenches you, and a garment that covers you" [252] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/369, commentary on the verse, no. 29334].

And with the same chain, from Mihran, from Sufyan, from Bakr ibn [ʿAtiq] al-ʿAmiri, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr was brought a cup of honey, and he said: "Indeed, this is among the bounties about which one will be questioned" [Ibid.].

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: it means: concerning what He has bestowed upon you through Muhammad (ﷺ). The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿They recognize the favour of God, then they deny it﴾ [Qur'an 16:83].

ʿIkrima said: (it means) concerning health and leisure.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: (it means) concerning health, leisure and wealth. Its evidence is what Ibn ʿAbbas narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Two bounties, in which many people are deceived: health and leisure" [253] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/344].

ʿUrwa ibn Muhammad said: We were with Wahb ibn Munabbih, and we saw a man who was deaf, blind, paralysed, leprous and afflicted, so we said: "Is there still any bounty left for this man?" He said: "Yes. Its greatest part is that he is satisfied with what he eats and drinks, and it is easy for him when he goes out to relieve himself."

Bakr, from ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani, said: "What a bounty: he eats with pleasure and expels waste with ease!" Abu al-ʿAliya said: (it means) concerning Islam and concealment (of sins). al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: the lightening of the laws and the facilitation of the Qur'an. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: (it means) concerning the blessings and the favours.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 102, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Meccan, and it has one hundred and twenty letters, twenty-eight words, and eight verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qathm informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Matar related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from my father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ will not be called to account for the blessings that were bestowed upon him in the abode of this world, and he will be given a reward as if he had recited a thousand verses." [239] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/430.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾: it means, the pursuit of boasting and vying in the abundance of wealth and numbers has preoccupied you from obeying your Lord and from what would save you from His wrath, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, that is, until you die and are buried in them.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, who said: "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so," and this distracted them until they died in error. Ibn Buraydah said: It was revealed concerning a clan of the Ansar who boasted. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning two tribes of Quraysh: Banu 'Abd Manaf and Banu Qusayy, and Banu Sahm ibn 'Amr ibn Husays ibn Ka'b. A dispute arose between them, so they counted their chiefs and nobles to see which of them was more numerous. Banu 'Abd Manaf said: "We are more numerous in chiefs, mightier in might, greater in company, and more in number."

Banu Sahm said the same, so Banu 'Abd Manaf outnumbered them. Then they said: "Let us count our dead," so they went to the graves and counted them, saying: "This is the grave of so-and-so, and this is the grave of so-and-so." Banu Sahm outnumbered them by three houses, because they had been more numerous in the Jahiliyyah. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far and Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Habariyan informed us, both saying: Abu Muhammad Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn [Sufyan] informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Musayyib related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl related to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Nakhir, from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) while he was reciting this verse: ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾. He said: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' But do you have of your wealth anything except what you eat and consume, or what you wear and wear out, or what you give in charity and send ahead?"

Zirr ibn Hubaysh narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ was revealed, up to ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, meaning in the grave.

﴿No! You will come to know﴾: a warning to them. ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾: the repetition is for emphasis. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾ refers to the believers. He used to recite it thus: the first with the letter ta' and the second with the letter ya'.

﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾, that is, knowledge that is certain. He attributed knowledge to certainty, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: 95.]]. Qatadah said: We used to narrate that the knowledge of certainty is to know that Allah will resurrect him after death.

﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. It may be that this, in the sense of the past tense, is the answer to "if" (law), its meaning being: If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would have seen Hell with your hearts, and then you would have seen it with the eye of certainty.

It was also said: Its meaning is: If you knew with certain knowledge, it would have preoccupied you from abundance and boasting. Then he resumed with ﴿You will surely see Hellfire﴾ in the sense of an oath, and Muqatil took this view. It was also said: Its meaning is: If you knew with certainty that you would see the Fire, that would have preoccupied you from what you are engaged in.

It was also said: He mentioned "no" three times, meaning: you will know at the moment of death, you will know in the grave, and you will know on the Day of Resurrection. Then in the third he mentioned the knowledge of certainty, because what had been unseen became a direct witnessing.

The reading of the common reciters is ﴿لَتُرَوُنَّ﴾ with a ḍammah on the tā' in both places. Al-Kisa'i put a ḍammah on the tā' in the first of them and a fatḥah on the second, and he transmitted this from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm related to us, saying: al-Farra' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed me, from 'Ata', from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, that he recited ﴿لَتُرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ﴾ and ﴿ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا﴾ with a ḍammah on the first tā' and a fatḥah on the second. Al-Farra' said: The first is more in keeping with the speech of the Arabs, because it is an intensification, and its pronunciation should not vary.

﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾. They differed concerning it and said much.

Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Sarraj informed us, by my reading to him in the Jami' on Friday in Muharram of the year 388, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mihran al-Khashshab related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Mu'adh al-Akhfash, the dictator (mustamli) of Abu Hafs al-Fallas, related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi Suwayd al-Dhari' related to us, saying: Suwayd Abu Hatim related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sufyan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "About cold water." [240] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/391.]]

And Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Qayyim al-Hasani al-Sunni related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahdi ibn Sadaqah related to us in Ramla, saying: My father related to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida related to us, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far related to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: My father Muhammad ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: My father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: "Fresh dates and cold water." [[Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn: 5/665.]]

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: It is cold water in summer. The evidence for this interpretation is the transmitted report: "The first thing Allah, the Exalted, will ask the servant about on the Day of Resurrection is that He will say to him: 'Did I not make your body healthy and give you to drink of cold water?'" [241] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/26, and Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/254, no. 6416, with slight variation.]]

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a guest of al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who brought food before him, and he ate it, then gave him cold water to drink, and he found it pleasant and said: "How cool it is for the liver!" Then he said: "When one of you drinks water, let him drink the coolest that he can obtain." It was asked: Why? He said: "It is better for the stomach, more beneficial for illness, and more inspiring of gratitude." [242] [[Subul al-Huda wa al-Rashad: 12/104, quoting the author.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari say: I heard Abu al-'Abbas al-Azhari say: I heard Abu Hatim say: Cold, sweet water draws praise out from the depths of the heart.

Malik ibn Dinar said: A man said to al-Hasan: "We have a neighbour who does not eat sweet pastry (faludh) and says: 'I cannot give thanks for it.'" He said: "How ignorant your neighbour is of Allah's blessing upon him in cold water, which is greater than the blessing of all sweets!"

Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad [ibn Muhammad al-Rumi] informed us, saying: Abu Hafs Muhammad ibn Hafs al-Basri related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah ibn 'Ayyash related to us, saying: al-Ash'ath ibn Nizar related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (peace be upon him), concerning the saying of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, said: "Whoever eats wheat bread, drinks cold water, and has shade, that is the bliss he will be questioned about." [243] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/39.]] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/555, no. 4715, and Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388, at the verse, and in it: "and drinks the water of the Euphrates cold, and has a dwelling he lives in."]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik related to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Shuja' related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Isbahani related to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "Security and health." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/365.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Barzah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn Harb related to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Raqashi al-Minqari related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa ibn Khalaf related to us, saying: Yunus ibn 'Abd related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came out to us at midday and found Abu Bakr in the mosque, and said: "O Abu Bakr, what has brought you out at this hour?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what brought you out has brought me out."

He said: 'Umar came and the Messenger of Allah said to him: "O Abu al-Khattab, what has brought you out?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what brought you both out." 'Umar sat with them. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began to converse with them, then said: "Do you have the strength to go to this palm grove, where you may find food, drink, and shade?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Pass by us to Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan al-Ansari." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went ahead of us, asked permission, and greeted them three times, while Umm al-Haytham was listening to the speech from behind the door, wishing that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would increase their greeting. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) wished to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out running after them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I heard your greeting, but I wished that you would give us more of your greeting."

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to her: "Where is Abu al-Haytham?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is nearby; he has gone to fetch us sweet water. Enter, for he will come at once, God willing."

She spread a carpet for them under a tree until Abu al-Haytham came. Abu al-Haytham rejoiced at them and his eye was refreshed. Abu al-Haytham climbed a palm tree to cut a cluster for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you eat of its unripe and its ripe dates, and its tadhnub [[al-Tadhnub: the part of the date cluster where ripening begins from its tail end.]]." Then he came to them, and they drank over it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bliss about which you will be questioned."

Then Abu al-Haytham got up to a sheep they had to slaughter it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milk-giving one." Umm al-Haytham stood to knead and bake for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and 'Umar placed their heads down for a midday rest. They woke up, and their food was ready, so the food was placed before them, and they ate and were satisfied and praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then Abu al-Haytham returned to them the remaining clusters, and they ate from its ripe dates [and from its tadhnub]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) greeted them and invoked good for them. [244] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 19/254; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/317; and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 1/215, no. 250.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Mu'adhdhin, who is Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Wadda', related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, about what bliss will we be questioned, when there are only these two black things, dates and water, and our swords are on our shoulders?" He said: "That will indeed occur." [245] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/142, with slight variation.]]

Al-Fanjawi informed us, saying: al-Qatay'i related to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Affan related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Yusuf, the son of the sister of Ibn Sirin, informed us, from Abu Qilabah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "Some people of my community will mix ghee and honey with pure flour and eat it." [246] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388; and Fath al-Qadir: 5/490.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Haytham informed us, saying: Mansur ibn Zadhan informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Let him not enter the bathhouse, for it is among the blessings that they have invented." He said: Mansur used not to enter the bathhouse.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: [Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan] related to us, saying: Mahmud [[He narrated it in other places as Ahmad ibn al-Faraj.]] ibn al-Faraj related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah related to us, from Ibrahim al-Hajari, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, will enumerate His blessings upon the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He enumerates them to him: 'Did so-and-so ask me to marry her to you?' — naming her by her name — 'and I married her to you.'" [247] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/177.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Khasib related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Isa related to me, saying: Fadl ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾ was revealed, the Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, what bliss are we in? We eat only to half-fill our bellies?" Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to His Prophet: "Say to them: 'Do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? That is of the bliss.'" [248] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/584; and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Ashnani the judge related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id al-Kharraz related to us, saying: My father related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to me, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾ was revealed, a needy man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there any blessing upon me?" He said: "Yes: the two sandals, the shade, and cold water." [249] [[Dhikr Akhbar Isbahan: 2/277, where it reads "al-Dhilal" instead of "al-Dhill".]]

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Hani' informed us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Rawasani related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: About every pleasure of the pleasures of this world.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi 'Isa related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abu 'Amir ibn Asaf al-Yamami related to us, from Yahya, who was a slave of Ibn Abi Kathir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ to his Companions, and when he reached ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, he said: "Do you know what that bliss is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "A house that shelters you, a cloth that covers your nakedness, and a morsel that keeps your back upright; anything beyond that is bliss." [250] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 20/176, with variation.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us by licence, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Makki informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Muqri' at Shamshat related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Sufyan ibn 'Alqamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muqaddami related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Khalid related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ and said: "The abundance of wealth: gathering it from other than its rightful source, withholding it from its rightful due, and tying it up in containers; ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, until you enter your graves; ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, if you enter your graves; ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾, if you come out of your graves to your place of gathering; ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾, when the scrolls are scattered, whether wretched or fortunate; ﴿You will surely see Hellfire, then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾" — he said: "And that is when it is brought up with the Sirat, set between the two pits of Hell" — ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: he said: "About five: about the fullness of the belly, the coolness of drink, the sweetness of sleep, the shade of dwellings, and the soundness of bodily constitution." [251]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: Abu Khalad al-Ahmar related to us, from Mufaddal, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: Whoever eats, mentions the name of Allah, and finishes, then praises Allah, will not be questioned about the bliss of that food.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "al-Naʿim" (the bounty) is the health of the bodies, the hearing and the sight. He said: God will question the servants about how they used them, and He knows that better than they do. This is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned about﴾ [Qur'an 17:36].

Abu Jaʿfar said: it is well-being (al-ʿafiya).

ʿAqil informed me, saying: al-Muʿafa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Ibn Humayd informed us, saying: Mihran narrated to us from Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi, from Thabit al-Bunani, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The bounty that will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection is a morsel of bread that sustains you, water that quenches you, and a garment that covers you" [252] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/369, commentary on the verse, no. 29334].

And with the same chain, from Mihran, from Sufyan, from Bakr ibn [ʿAtiq] al-ʿAmiri, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr was brought a cup of honey, and he said: "Indeed, this is among the bounties about which one will be questioned" [Ibid.].

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: it means: concerning what He has bestowed upon you through Muhammad (ﷺ). The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿They recognize the favour of God, then they deny it﴾ [Qur'an 16:83].

ʿIkrima said: (it means) concerning health and leisure.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: (it means) concerning health, leisure and wealth. Its evidence is what Ibn ʿAbbas narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Two bounties, in which many people are deceived: health and leisure" [253] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/344].

ʿUrwa ibn Muhammad said: We were with Wahb ibn Munabbih, and we saw a man who was deaf, blind, paralysed, leprous and afflicted, so we said: "Is there still any bounty left for this man?" He said: "Yes. Its greatest part is that he is satisfied with what he eats and drinks, and it is easy for him when he goes out to relieve himself."

Bakr, from ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani, said: "What a bounty: he eats with pleasure and expels waste with ease!" Abu al-ʿAliya said: (it means) concerning Islam and concealment (of sins). al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: the lightening of the laws and the facilitation of the Qur'an. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: (it means) concerning the blessings and the favours.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 102, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Meccan, and it has one hundred and twenty letters, twenty-eight words, and eight verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qathm informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Matar related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from my father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ will not be called to account for the blessings that were bestowed upon him in the abode of this world, and he will be given a reward as if he had recited a thousand verses." [239] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/430.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾: it means, the pursuit of boasting and vying in the abundance of wealth and numbers has preoccupied you from obeying your Lord and from what would save you from His wrath, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, that is, until you die and are buried in them.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, who said: "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so," and this distracted them until they died in error. Ibn Buraydah said: It was revealed concerning a clan of the Ansar who boasted. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning two tribes of Quraysh: Banu 'Abd Manaf and Banu Qusayy, and Banu Sahm ibn 'Amr ibn Husays ibn Ka'b. A dispute arose between them, so they counted their chiefs and nobles to see which of them was more numerous. Banu 'Abd Manaf said: "We are more numerous in chiefs, mightier in might, greater in company, and more in number."

Banu Sahm said the same, so Banu 'Abd Manaf outnumbered them. Then they said: "Let us count our dead," so they went to the graves and counted them, saying: "This is the grave of so-and-so, and this is the grave of so-and-so." Banu Sahm outnumbered them by three houses, because they had been more numerous in the Jahiliyyah. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far and Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Habariyan informed us, both saying: Abu Muhammad Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn [Sufyan] informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Musayyib related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl related to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Nakhir, from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) while he was reciting this verse: ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾. He said: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' But do you have of your wealth anything except what you eat and consume, or what you wear and wear out, or what you give in charity and send ahead?"

Zirr ibn Hubaysh narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ was revealed, up to ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, meaning in the grave.

﴿No! You will come to know﴾: a warning to them. ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾: the repetition is for emphasis. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾ refers to the believers. He used to recite it thus: the first with the letter ta' and the second with the letter ya'.

﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾, that is, knowledge that is certain. He attributed knowledge to certainty, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: 95.]]. Qatadah said: We used to narrate that the knowledge of certainty is to know that Allah will resurrect him after death.

﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. It may be that this, in the sense of the past tense, is the answer to "if" (law), its meaning being: If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would have seen Hell with your hearts, and then you would have seen it with the eye of certainty.

It was also said: Its meaning is: If you knew with certain knowledge, it would have preoccupied you from abundance and boasting. Then he resumed with ﴿You will surely see Hellfire﴾ in the sense of an oath, and Muqatil took this view. It was also said: Its meaning is: If you knew with certainty that you would see the Fire, that would have preoccupied you from what you are engaged in.

It was also said: He mentioned "no" three times, meaning: you will know at the moment of death, you will know in the grave, and you will know on the Day of Resurrection. Then in the third he mentioned the knowledge of certainty, because what had been unseen became a direct witnessing.

The reading of the common reciters is ﴿لَتُرَوُنَّ﴾ with a ḍammah on the tā' in both places. Al-Kisa'i put a ḍammah on the tā' in the first of them and a fatḥah on the second, and he transmitted this from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm related to us, saying: al-Farra' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed me, from 'Ata', from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, that he recited ﴿لَتُرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ﴾ and ﴿ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا﴾ with a ḍammah on the first tā' and a fatḥah on the second. Al-Farra' said: The first is more in keeping with the speech of the Arabs, because it is an intensification, and its pronunciation should not vary.

﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾. They differed concerning it and said much.

Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Sarraj informed us, by my reading to him in the Jami' on Friday in Muharram of the year 388, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mihran al-Khashshab related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Mu'adh al-Akhfash, the dictator (mustamli) of Abu Hafs al-Fallas, related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi Suwayd al-Dhari' related to us, saying: Suwayd Abu Hatim related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sufyan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "About cold water." [240] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/391.]]

And Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Qayyim al-Hasani al-Sunni related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahdi ibn Sadaqah related to us in Ramla, saying: My father related to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida related to us, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far related to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: My father Muhammad ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: My father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: "Fresh dates and cold water." [[Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn: 5/665.]]

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: It is cold water in summer. The evidence for this interpretation is the transmitted report: "The first thing Allah, the Exalted, will ask the servant about on the Day of Resurrection is that He will say to him: 'Did I not make your body healthy and give you to drink of cold water?'" [241] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/26, and Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/254, no. 6416, with slight variation.]]

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a guest of al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who brought food before him, and he ate it, then gave him cold water to drink, and he found it pleasant and said: "How cool it is for the liver!" Then he said: "When one of you drinks water, let him drink the coolest that he can obtain." It was asked: Why? He said: "It is better for the stomach, more beneficial for illness, and more inspiring of gratitude." [242] [[Subul al-Huda wa al-Rashad: 12/104, quoting the author.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari say: I heard Abu al-'Abbas al-Azhari say: I heard Abu Hatim say: Cold, sweet water draws praise out from the depths of the heart.

Malik ibn Dinar said: A man said to al-Hasan: "We have a neighbour who does not eat sweet pastry (faludh) and says: 'I cannot give thanks for it.'" He said: "How ignorant your neighbour is of Allah's blessing upon him in cold water, which is greater than the blessing of all sweets!"

Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad [ibn Muhammad al-Rumi] informed us, saying: Abu Hafs Muhammad ibn Hafs al-Basri related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah ibn 'Ayyash related to us, saying: al-Ash'ath ibn Nizar related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (peace be upon him), concerning the saying of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, said: "Whoever eats wheat bread, drinks cold water, and has shade, that is the bliss he will be questioned about." [243] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/39.]] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/555, no. 4715, and Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388, at the verse, and in it: "and drinks the water of the Euphrates cold, and has a dwelling he lives in."]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik related to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Shuja' related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Isbahani related to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "Security and health." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/365.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Barzah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn Harb related to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Raqashi al-Minqari related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa ibn Khalaf related to us, saying: Yunus ibn 'Abd related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came out to us at midday and found Abu Bakr in the mosque, and said: "O Abu Bakr, what has brought you out at this hour?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what brought you out has brought me out."

He said: 'Umar came and the Messenger of Allah said to him: "O Abu al-Khattab, what has brought you out?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what brought you both out." 'Umar sat with them. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began to converse with them, then said: "Do you have the strength to go to this palm grove, where you may find food, drink, and shade?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Pass by us to Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan al-Ansari." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went ahead of us, asked permission, and greeted them three times, while Umm al-Haytham was listening to the speech from behind the door, wishing that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would increase their greeting. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) wished to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out running after them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I heard your greeting, but I wished that you would give us more of your greeting."

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to her: "Where is Abu al-Haytham?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is nearby; he has gone to fetch us sweet water. Enter, for he will come at once, God willing."

She spread a carpet for them under a tree until Abu al-Haytham came. Abu al-Haytham rejoiced at them and his eye was refreshed. Abu al-Haytham climbed a palm tree to cut a cluster for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you eat of its unripe and its ripe dates, and its tadhnub [[al-Tadhnub: the part of the date cluster where ripening begins from its tail end.]]." Then he came to them, and they drank over it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bliss about which you will be questioned."

Then Abu al-Haytham got up to a sheep they had to slaughter it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milk-giving one." Umm al-Haytham stood to knead and bake for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and 'Umar placed their heads down for a midday rest. They woke up, and their food was ready, so the food was placed before them, and they ate and were satisfied and praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then Abu al-Haytham returned to them the remaining clusters, and they ate from its ripe dates [and from its tadhnub]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) greeted them and invoked good for them. [244] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 19/254; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/317; and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 1/215, no. 250.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Mu'adhdhin, who is Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Wadda', related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, about what bliss will we be questioned, when there are only these two black things, dates and water, and our swords are on our shoulders?" He said: "That will indeed occur." [245] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/142, with slight variation.]]

Al-Fanjawi informed us, saying: al-Qatay'i related to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Affan related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Yusuf, the son of the sister of Ibn Sirin, informed us, from Abu Qilabah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "Some people of my community will mix ghee and honey with pure flour and eat it." [246] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388; and Fath al-Qadir: 5/490.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Haytham informed us, saying: Mansur ibn Zadhan informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Let him not enter the bathhouse, for it is among the blessings that they have invented." He said: Mansur used not to enter the bathhouse.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: [Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan] related to us, saying: Mahmud [[He narrated it in other places as Ahmad ibn al-Faraj.]] ibn al-Faraj related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah related to us, from Ibrahim al-Hajari, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, will enumerate His blessings upon the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He enumerates them to him: 'Did so-and-so ask me to marry her to you?' — naming her by her name — 'and I married her to you.'" [247] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/177.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Khasib related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Isa related to me, saying: Fadl ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾ was revealed, the Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, what bliss are we in? We eat only to half-fill our bellies?" Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to His Prophet: "Say to them: 'Do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? That is of the bliss.'" [248] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/584; and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Ashnani the judge related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id al-Kharraz related to us, saying: My father related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to me, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾ was revealed, a needy man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there any blessing upon me?" He said: "Yes: the two sandals, the shade, and cold water." [249] [[Dhikr Akhbar Isbahan: 2/277, where it reads "al-Dhilal" instead of "al-Dhill".]]

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Hani' informed us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Rawasani related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: About every pleasure of the pleasures of this world.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi 'Isa related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abu 'Amir ibn Asaf al-Yamami related to us, from Yahya, who was a slave of Ibn Abi Kathir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ to his Companions, and when he reached ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, he said: "Do you know what that bliss is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "A house that shelters you, a cloth that covers your nakedness, and a morsel that keeps your back upright; anything beyond that is bliss." [250] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 20/176, with variation.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us by licence, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Makki informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Muqri' at Shamshat related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Sufyan ibn 'Alqamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muqaddami related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Khalid related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ and said: "The abundance of wealth: gathering it from other than its rightful source, withholding it from its rightful due, and tying it up in containers; ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, until you enter your graves; ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, if you enter your graves; ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾, if you come out of your graves to your place of gathering; ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾, when the scrolls are scattered, whether wretched or fortunate; ﴿You will surely see Hellfire, then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾" — he said: "And that is when it is brought up with the Sirat, set between the two pits of Hell" — ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: he said: "About five: about the fullness of the belly, the coolness of drink, the sweetness of sleep, the shade of dwellings, and the soundness of bodily constitution." [251]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: Abu Khalad al-Ahmar related to us, from Mufaddal, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: Whoever eats, mentions the name of Allah, and finishes, then praises Allah, will not be questioned about the bliss of that food.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "al-Naʿim" (the bounty) is the health of the bodies, the hearing and the sight. He said: God will question the servants about how they used them, and He knows that better than they do. This is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned about﴾ [Qur'an 17:36].

Abu Jaʿfar said: it is well-being (al-ʿafiya).

ʿAqil informed me, saying: al-Muʿafa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Ibn Humayd informed us, saying: Mihran narrated to us from Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi, from Thabit al-Bunani, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The bounty that will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection is a morsel of bread that sustains you, water that quenches you, and a garment that covers you" [252] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/369, commentary on the verse, no. 29334].

And with the same chain, from Mihran, from Sufyan, from Bakr ibn [ʿAtiq] al-ʿAmiri, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr was brought a cup of honey, and he said: "Indeed, this is among the bounties about which one will be questioned" [Ibid.].

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: it means: concerning what He has bestowed upon you through Muhammad (ﷺ). The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿They recognize the favour of God, then they deny it﴾ [Qur'an 16:83].

ʿIkrima said: (it means) concerning health and leisure.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: (it means) concerning health, leisure and wealth. Its evidence is what Ibn ʿAbbas narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Two bounties, in which many people are deceived: health and leisure" [253] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/344].

ʿUrwa ibn Muhammad said: We were with Wahb ibn Munabbih, and we saw a man who was deaf, blind, paralysed, leprous and afflicted, so we said: "Is there still any bounty left for this man?" He said: "Yes. Its greatest part is that he is satisfied with what he eats and drinks, and it is easy for him when he goes out to relieve himself."

Bakr, from ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani, said: "What a bounty: he eats with pleasure and expels waste with ease!" Abu al-ʿAliya said: (it means) concerning Islam and concealment (of sins). al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: the lightening of the laws and the facilitation of the Qur'an. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: (it means) concerning the blessings and the favours.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 102, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Meccan, and it has one hundred and twenty letters, twenty-eight words, and eight verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qathm informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Matar related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from my father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ will not be called to account for the blessings that were bestowed upon him in the abode of this world, and he will be given a reward as if he had recited a thousand verses." [239] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/430.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾: it means, the pursuit of boasting and vying in the abundance of wealth and numbers has preoccupied you from obeying your Lord and from what would save you from His wrath, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, that is, until you die and are buried in them.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, who said: "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so," and this distracted them until they died in error. Ibn Buraydah said: It was revealed concerning a clan of the Ansar who boasted. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning two tribes of Quraysh: Banu 'Abd Manaf and Banu Qusayy, and Banu Sahm ibn 'Amr ibn Husays ibn Ka'b. A dispute arose between them, so they counted their chiefs and nobles to see which of them was more numerous. Banu 'Abd Manaf said: "We are more numerous in chiefs, mightier in might, greater in company, and more in number."

Banu Sahm said the same, so Banu 'Abd Manaf outnumbered them. Then they said: "Let us count our dead," so they went to the graves and counted them, saying: "This is the grave of so-and-so, and this is the grave of so-and-so." Banu Sahm outnumbered them by three houses, because they had been more numerous in the Jahiliyyah. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far and Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Habariyan informed us, both saying: Abu Muhammad Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn [Sufyan] informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Musayyib related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl related to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Nakhir, from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) while he was reciting this verse: ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾. He said: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' But do you have of your wealth anything except what you eat and consume, or what you wear and wear out, or what you give in charity and send ahead?"

Zirr ibn Hubaysh narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ was revealed, up to ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, meaning in the grave.

﴿No! You will come to know﴾: a warning to them. ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾: the repetition is for emphasis. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾ refers to the believers. He used to recite it thus: the first with the letter ta' and the second with the letter ya'.

﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾, that is, knowledge that is certain. He attributed knowledge to certainty, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: 95.]]. Qatadah said: We used to narrate that the knowledge of certainty is to know that Allah will resurrect him after death.

﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. It may be that this, in the sense of the past tense, is the answer to "if" (law), its meaning being: If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would have seen Hell with your hearts, and then you would have seen it with the eye of certainty.

It was also said: Its meaning is: If you knew with certain knowledge, it would have preoccupied you from abundance and boasting. Then he resumed with ﴿You will surely see Hellfire﴾ in the sense of an oath, and Muqatil took this view. It was also said: Its meaning is: If you knew with certainty that you would see the Fire, that would have preoccupied you from what you are engaged in.

It was also said: He mentioned "no" three times, meaning: you will know at the moment of death, you will know in the grave, and you will know on the Day of Resurrection. Then in the third he mentioned the knowledge of certainty, because what had been unseen became a direct witnessing.

The reading of the common reciters is ﴿لَتُرَوُنَّ﴾ with a ḍammah on the tā' in both places. Al-Kisa'i put a ḍammah on the tā' in the first of them and a fatḥah on the second, and he transmitted this from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm related to us, saying: al-Farra' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed me, from 'Ata', from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, that he recited ﴿لَتُرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ﴾ and ﴿ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا﴾ with a ḍammah on the first tā' and a fatḥah on the second. Al-Farra' said: The first is more in keeping with the speech of the Arabs, because it is an intensification, and its pronunciation should not vary.

﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾. They differed concerning it and said much.

Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Sarraj informed us, by my reading to him in the Jami' on Friday in Muharram of the year 388, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mihran al-Khashshab related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Mu'adh al-Akhfash, the dictator (mustamli) of Abu Hafs al-Fallas, related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi Suwayd al-Dhari' related to us, saying: Suwayd Abu Hatim related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sufyan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "About cold water." [240] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/391.]]

And Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Qayyim al-Hasani al-Sunni related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahdi ibn Sadaqah related to us in Ramla, saying: My father related to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida related to us, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far related to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: My father Muhammad ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: My father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: "Fresh dates and cold water." [[Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn: 5/665.]]

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: It is cold water in summer. The evidence for this interpretation is the transmitted report: "The first thing Allah, the Exalted, will ask the servant about on the Day of Resurrection is that He will say to him: 'Did I not make your body healthy and give you to drink of cold water?'" [241] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/26, and Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/254, no. 6416, with slight variation.]]

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a guest of al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who brought food before him, and he ate it, then gave him cold water to drink, and he found it pleasant and said: "How cool it is for the liver!" Then he said: "When one of you drinks water, let him drink the coolest that he can obtain." It was asked: Why? He said: "It is better for the stomach, more beneficial for illness, and more inspiring of gratitude." [242] [[Subul al-Huda wa al-Rashad: 12/104, quoting the author.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari say: I heard Abu al-'Abbas al-Azhari say: I heard Abu Hatim say: Cold, sweet water draws praise out from the depths of the heart.

Malik ibn Dinar said: A man said to al-Hasan: "We have a neighbour who does not eat sweet pastry (faludh) and says: 'I cannot give thanks for it.'" He said: "How ignorant your neighbour is of Allah's blessing upon him in cold water, which is greater than the blessing of all sweets!"

Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad [ibn Muhammad al-Rumi] informed us, saying: Abu Hafs Muhammad ibn Hafs al-Basri related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah ibn 'Ayyash related to us, saying: al-Ash'ath ibn Nizar related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (peace be upon him), concerning the saying of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, said: "Whoever eats wheat bread, drinks cold water, and has shade, that is the bliss he will be questioned about." [243] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/39.]] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/555, no. 4715, and Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388, at the verse, and in it: "and drinks the water of the Euphrates cold, and has a dwelling he lives in."]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik related to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Shuja' related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Isbahani related to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "Security and health." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/365.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Barzah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn Harb related to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Raqashi al-Minqari related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa ibn Khalaf related to us, saying: Yunus ibn 'Abd related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came out to us at midday and found Abu Bakr in the mosque, and said: "O Abu Bakr, what has brought you out at this hour?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what brought you out has brought me out."

He said: 'Umar came and the Messenger of Allah said to him: "O Abu al-Khattab, what has brought you out?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what brought you both out." 'Umar sat with them. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began to converse with them, then said: "Do you have the strength to go to this palm grove, where you may find food, drink, and shade?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Pass by us to Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan al-Ansari." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went ahead of us, asked permission, and greeted them three times, while Umm al-Haytham was listening to the speech from behind the door, wishing that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would increase their greeting. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) wished to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out running after them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I heard your greeting, but I wished that you would give us more of your greeting."

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to her: "Where is Abu al-Haytham?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is nearby; he has gone to fetch us sweet water. Enter, for he will come at once, God willing."

She spread a carpet for them under a tree until Abu al-Haytham came. Abu al-Haytham rejoiced at them and his eye was refreshed. Abu al-Haytham climbed a palm tree to cut a cluster for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you eat of its unripe and its ripe dates, and its tadhnub [[al-Tadhnub: the part of the date cluster where ripening begins from its tail end.]]." Then he came to them, and they drank over it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bliss about which you will be questioned."

Then Abu al-Haytham got up to a sheep they had to slaughter it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milk-giving one." Umm al-Haytham stood to knead and bake for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and 'Umar placed their heads down for a midday rest. They woke up, and their food was ready, so the food was placed before them, and they ate and were satisfied and praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then Abu al-Haytham returned to them the remaining clusters, and they ate from its ripe dates [and from its tadhnub]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) greeted them and invoked good for them. [244] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 19/254; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/317; and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 1/215, no. 250.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Mu'adhdhin, who is Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Wadda', related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, about what bliss will we be questioned, when there are only these two black things, dates and water, and our swords are on our shoulders?" He said: "That will indeed occur." [245] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/142, with slight variation.]]

Al-Fanjawi informed us, saying: al-Qatay'i related to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Affan related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Yusuf, the son of the sister of Ibn Sirin, informed us, from Abu Qilabah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "Some people of my community will mix ghee and honey with pure flour and eat it." [246] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388; and Fath al-Qadir: 5/490.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah related to us, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Haytham informed us, saying: Mansur ibn Zadhan informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Let him not enter the bathhouse, for it is among the blessings that they have invented." He said: Mansur used not to enter the bathhouse.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: [Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan] related to us, saying: Mahmud [[He narrated it in other places as Ahmad ibn al-Faraj.]] ibn al-Faraj related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah related to us, from Ibrahim al-Hajari, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, will enumerate His blessings upon the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He enumerates them to him: 'Did so-and-so ask me to marry her to you?' — naming her by her name — 'and I married her to you.'" [247] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/177.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Khasib related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Isa related to me, saying: Fadl ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾ was revealed, the Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, what bliss are we in? We eat only to half-fill our bellies?" Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed to His Prophet: "Say to them: 'Do you not wear sandals and drink cold water? That is of the bliss.'" [248] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/584; and al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Zur'ah al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Ashnani the judge related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id al-Kharraz related to us, saying: My father related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan related to me, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾ was revealed, a needy man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there any blessing upon me?" He said: "Yes: the two sandals, the shade, and cold water." [249] [[Dhikr Akhbar Isbahan: 2/277, where it reads "al-Dhilal" instead of "al-Dhill".]]

Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Hani' informed us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Rawasani related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: About every pleasure of the pleasures of this world.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi 'Isa related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abu 'Amir ibn Asaf al-Yamami related to us, from Yahya, who was a slave of Ibn Abi Kathir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ to his Companions, and when he reached ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, he said: "Do you know what that bliss is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "A house that shelters you, a cloth that covers your nakedness, and a morsel that keeps your back upright; anything beyond that is bliss." [250] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 20/176, with variation.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us by licence, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Makki informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Muqri' at Shamshat related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Sufyan ibn 'Alqamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muqaddami related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Khalid related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ and said: "The abundance of wealth: gathering it from other than its rightful source, withholding it from its rightful due, and tying it up in containers; ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, until you enter your graves; ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, if you enter your graves; ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾, if you come out of your graves to your place of gathering; ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾, when the scrolls are scattered, whether wretched or fortunate; ﴿You will surely see Hellfire, then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾" — he said: "And that is when it is brought up with the Sirat, set between the two pits of Hell" — ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: he said: "About five: about the fullness of the belly, the coolness of drink, the sweetness of sleep, the shade of dwellings, and the soundness of bodily constitution." [251]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: Abu Khalad al-Ahmar related to us, from Mufaddal, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: Whoever eats, mentions the name of Allah, and finishes, then praises Allah, will not be questioned about the bliss of that food.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "al-Naʿim" (the bounty) is the health of the bodies, the hearing and the sight. He said: God will question the servants about how they used them, and He knows that better than they do. This is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — all of those will be questioned about﴾ [Qur'an 17:36].

Abu Jaʿfar said: it is well-being (al-ʿafiya).

ʿAqil informed me, saying: al-Muʿafa informed us, saying: Ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Ibn Humayd informed us, saying: Mihran narrated to us from Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi, from Thabit al-Bunani, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The bounty that will be questioned about on the Day of Resurrection is a morsel of bread that sustains you, water that quenches you, and a garment that covers you" [252] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/369, commentary on the verse, no. 29334].

And with the same chain, from Mihran, from Sufyan, from Bakr ibn [ʿAtiq] al-ʿAmiri, who said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr was brought a cup of honey, and he said: "Indeed, this is among the bounties about which one will be questioned" [Ibid.].

Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: it means: concerning what He has bestowed upon you through Muhammad (ﷺ). The evidence for this interpretation is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿They recognize the favour of God, then they deny it﴾ [Qur'an 16:83].

ʿIkrima said: (it means) concerning health and leisure.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: (it means) concerning health, leisure and wealth. Its evidence is what Ibn ʿAbbas narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Two bounties, in which many people are deceived: health and leisure" [253] [Musnad Ahmad: 1/344].

ʿUrwa ibn Muhammad said: We were with Wahb ibn Munabbih, and we saw a man who was deaf, blind, paralysed, leprous and afflicted, so we said: "Is there still any bounty left for this man?" He said: "Yes. Its greatest part is that he is satisfied with what he eats and drinks, and it is easy for him when he goes out to relieve himself."

Bakr, from ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani, said: "What a bounty: he eats with pleasure and expels waste with ease!" Abu al-ʿAliya said: (it means) concerning Islam and concealment (of sins). al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: the lightening of the laws and the facilitation of the Qur'an. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: (it means) concerning the blessings and the favours.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 102, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Meccan, and it has one hundred and twenty letters, twenty-eight words, and eight verses.

Muhammad ibn al-Qathm informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Matar related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from my father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ will not be called to account for the blessings that were bestowed upon him in the abode of this world, and he will be given a reward as if he had recited a thousand verses." [239] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/430.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾: it means, the pursuit of boasting and vying in the abundance of wealth and numbers has preoccupied you from obeying your Lord and from what would save you from His wrath, ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, that is, until you die and are buried in them.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, who said: "We are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so, and the sons of so-and-so are more numerous than the sons of so-and-so," and this distracted them until they died in error. Ibn Buraydah said: It was revealed concerning a clan of the Ansar who boasted. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning two tribes of Quraysh: Banu 'Abd Manaf and Banu Qusayy, and Banu Sahm ibn 'Amr ibn Husays ibn Ka'b. A dispute arose between them, so they counted their chiefs and nobles to see which of them was more numerous. Banu 'Abd Manaf said: "We are more numerous in chiefs, mightier in might, greater in company, and more in number."

Banu Sahm said the same, so Banu 'Abd Manaf outnumbered them. Then they said: "Let us count our dead," so they went to the graves and counted them, saying: "This is the grave of so-and-so, and this is the grave of so-and-so." Banu Sahm outnumbered them by three houses, because they had been more numerous in the Jahiliyyah. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far and Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Habariyan informed us, both saying: Abu Muhammad Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn [Sufyan] informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Musayyib related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl related to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from Qatadah, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Nakhir, from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) while he was reciting this verse: ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾. He said: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' But do you have of your wealth anything except what you eat and consume, or what you wear and wear out, or what you give in charity and send ahead?"

Zirr ibn Hubaysh narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until ﴿Your abundance diverts you﴾ was revealed, up to ﴿No! You will come to know﴾, meaning in the grave.

﴿No! You will come to know﴾: a warning to them. ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾: the repetition is for emphasis. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿No! You will come to know﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and ﴿Then, no! You will come to know﴾ refers to the believers. He used to recite it thus: the first with the letter ta' and the second with the letter ya'.

﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾, that is, knowledge that is certain. He attributed knowledge to certainty, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is the truth of certainty﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: 95.]]. Qatadah said: We used to narrate that the knowledge of certainty is to know that Allah will resurrect him after death.

﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. It may be that this, in the sense of the past tense, is the answer to "if" (law), its meaning being: If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would have seen Hell with your hearts, and then you would have seen it with the eye of certainty.

It was also said: Its meaning is: If you knew with certain knowledge, it would have preoccupied you from abundance and boasting. Then he resumed with ﴿You will surely see Hellfire﴾ in the sense of an oath, and Muqatil took this view. It was also said: Its meaning is: If you knew with certainty that you would see the Fire, that would have preoccupied you from what you are engaged in.

It was also said: He mentioned "no" three times, meaning: you will know at the moment of death, you will know in the grave, and you will know on the Day of Resurrection. Then in the third he mentioned the knowledge of certainty, because what had been unseen became a direct witnessing.

The reading of the common reciters is ﴿لَتُرَوُنَّ﴾ with a ḍammah on the tā' in both places. Al-Kisa'i put a ḍammah on the tā' in the first of them and a fatḥah on the second, and he transmitted this from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm related to us, saying: al-Farra' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed me, from 'Ata', from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, that he recited ﴿لَتُرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ﴾ and ﴿ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا﴾ with a ḍammah on the first tā' and a fatḥah on the second. Al-Farra' said: The first is more in keeping with the speech of the Arabs, because it is an intensification, and its pronunciation should not vary.

﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾. They differed concerning it and said much.

Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Sarraj informed us, by my reading to him in the Jami' on Friday in Muharram of the year 388, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mihran al-Khashshab related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-'Askari related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Mu'adh al-Akhfash, the dictator (mustamli) of Abu Hafs al-Fallas, related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi Suwayd al-Dhari' related to us, saying: Suwayd Abu Hatim related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sufyan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "About cold water." [240] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/391.]]

And Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Qayyim al-Hasani al-Sunni related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahdi ibn Sadaqah related to us in Ramla, saying: My father related to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida related to us, saying: My father Musa ibn Ja'far related to me, saying: My father Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: My father Muhammad ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: My father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali related to me, saying: My father 'Ali ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾: "Fresh dates and cold water." [[Tafsir Nur al-Thaqalayn: 5/665.]]

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: It is cold water in summer. The evidence for this interpretation is the transmitted report: "The first thing Allah, the Exalted, will ask the servant about on the Day of Resurrection is that He will say to him: 'Did I not make your body healthy and give you to drink of cold water?'" [241] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/26, and Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/254, no. 6416, with slight variation.]]

Anas ibn Malik said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a guest of al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who brought food before him, and he ate it, then gave him cold water to drink, and he found it pleasant and said: "How cool it is for the liver!" Then he said: "When one of you drinks water, let him drink the coolest that he can obtain." It was asked: Why? He said: "It is better for the stomach, more beneficial for illness, and more inspiring of gratitude." [242] [[Subul al-Huda wa al-Rashad: 12/104, quoting the author.]]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-'Anbari say: I heard Abu al-'Abbas al-Azhari say: I heard Abu Hatim say: Cold, sweet water draws praise out from the depths of the heart.

Malik ibn Dinar said: A man said to al-Hasan: "We have a neighbour who does not eat sweet pastry (faludh) and says: 'I cannot give thanks for it.'" He said: "How ignorant your neighbour is of Allah's blessing upon him in cold water, which is greater than the blessing of all sweets!"

Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad [ibn Muhammad al-Rumi] informed us, saying: Abu Hafs Muhammad ibn Hafs al-Basri related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah ibn 'Ayyash related to us, saying: al-Ash'ath ibn Nizar related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (peace be upon him), concerning the saying of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, said: "Whoever eats wheat bread, drinks cold water, and has shade, that is the bliss he will be questioned about." [243] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/39.]] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 2/555, no. 4715, and Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/388, at the verse, and in it: "and drinks the water of the Euphrates cold, and has a dwelling he lives in."]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Malik related to us, saying: Ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Shuja' related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Isbahani related to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning ﴿Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the bliss﴾, that he said: "Security and health." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/365.]]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Barzah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib ibn Harb related to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Raqashi al-Minqari related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa ibn Khalaf related to us, saying: Yunus ibn 'Abd related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) came out to us at midday and found Abu Bakr in the mosque, and said: "O Abu Bakr, what has brought you out at this hour?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what brought you out has brought me out."

He said: 'Umar came and the Messenger of Allah said to him: "O Abu al-Khattab, what has brought you out?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what brought you both out." 'Umar sat with them. He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) began to converse with them, then said: "Do you have the strength to go to this palm grove, where you may find food, drink, and shade?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Pass by us to Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan al-Ansari." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went ahead of us, asked permission, and greeted them three times, while Umm al-Haytham was listening to the speech from behind the door, wishing that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would increase their greeting. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) wished to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out running after them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I heard your greeting, but I wished that you would give us more of your greeting."

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to her: "Where is Abu al-Haytham?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is nearby; he has gone to fetch us sweet water. Enter, for he will come at once, God willing."

She spread a carpet for them under a tree until Abu al-Haytham came. Abu al-Haytham rejoiced at them and his eye was refreshed. Abu al-Haytham climbed a palm tree to cut a cluster for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you eat of its unripe and its ripe dates, and its tadhnub [[al-Tadhnub: the part of the date cluster where ripening begins from its tail end.]]." Then he came to them, and they drank over it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is of the bliss about which you will be questioned."

Then Abu al-Haytham got up to a sheep they had to slaughter it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the milk-giving one." Umm al-Haytham stood to knead and bake for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and 'Umar placed their heads down for a midday rest. They woke up, and their food was ready, so the food was placed before them, and they ate and were satisfied and praised Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Then Abu al-Haytham returned to them the remaining clusters, and they ate from its ripe dates [and from its tadhnub]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) greeted them and invoked good for them.
